## What it is

CyberChef is a web page full of small data tools: Base64 and hex, hashes, encryption, compression, timestamps, regular expressions and hundreds more. You chain them into a "recipe" and see the result as you type ([gchq/CyberChef](https://github.com/gchq/CyberChef)). It is part of the Supply Depot (issue #129, NMD-04): the offline toolbox a box keeps for when the internet is gone.

**Licence:** `Apache-2.0` (GitHub licence API, and the image's own `org.opencontainers.image.licenses` label). Market class **L1**. The research licence matrix has a v11.5.0 row (`research-output/evidence/license-matrix.csv`), so the licence gate can confirm it.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with an initial; no upstream logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment`, one container: upstream's own image `ghcr.io/gchq/cyberchef`, which is nginx (unprivileged build, UID 101, port 8080) serving the built web page.
- **Why it is safe to run locked down:** every operation runs in your browser. The server only hands out static files and stores nothing, so it needs no volume and no write access to its own files.
- Read-only root filesystem with two small scratch volumes (`/var/cache/nginx`, `/tmp`) because nginx writes its temporary files and pid file there. Non-root (UID 101), RuntimeDefault seccomp, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, no service-account token.
- Probes: `GET /`.
- Image pinned by tag and digest (`11.5.0@sha256:f04a3992…`), read from the ghcr.io registry API (v2 manifest endpoint, anonymous token) on 2026-11-19; the index has amd64 and arm64.

## First run

Source: [CyberChef README](https://github.com/gchq/CyberChef#readme).

1. Install CyberChef from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-cyberchef`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:8080:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-cyberchef port-forward svc/cyberchef 8080:8080
   ```
3. Drag operations from the left into the recipe, paste data into the input box, and read the output.

## Not done yet

- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the app is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` is a claim the CI app gate checks; it moves to `verified` or `blocked` only through `sdk/tools/app-gate`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

**Pin bump (ma/market-bump-45-blocked-app-images, 2026-11-27, Refs #1232, Refs #234):** CyberChef 11.5.0 to 11.6.0. No breaking change found in the release notes. The new pins were read from the registries with `crane`. They were **not** scanned: the Trivy vulnerability database could not be downloaded from the build sandbox, so this change claims no pass. The tier stays `blocked`; the CI gate decides.
